problem: Multi-hop question answering struggles with effective retrieval across documents, leading to incomplete or inaccurate answers when integrating information from multiple sources.
method: Enhance Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Graph RAG) by constructing individual knowledge graphs for each document (entities as nodes, relationships as edges enriched with contextual properties), integrating them into a unified graph capturing cross-document relationships, and utilizing vector embeddings of graph relations for improved retrieval and multi-hop reasoning.
key_assumptions: Document-level knowledge graphs can be effectively integrated into a unified cross-document graph.
Vector embeddings of graph relations improve retrieval accuracy for multi-hop QA.
main_contribution: A novel graph-based retrieval mechanism leveraging vector embeddings of graph relations within the Graph RAG framework, plus a dataset of 500 documents and 296 multi-hop questions requiring cross-document information retrieval.
datasets: 296 multi-hop questions requiring cross-document information retrieval
results: ["Significantly outperforms baseline in factual accuracy and semantic similarity; superior performance in answer comprehensiveness, empowerment, and directness."]

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: This work focuses on constructing document-level knowledge graphs and using vector embeddings of relations for retrieval-augmented generation. Our idea enriches each target triple with local context subgraphs from the same passage and adds an adaptive repair loop for one-hop failures, targeting the training data and iterative correction rather than document-level KG integration for retrieval.
